about: Object taxonomy: domain > class > kind. Each entry inherits every field from its parent; parts+ and connections+ extend the inherited list, the other fields replace it. Parts: name, required, count, side (left/right pairs), sub_object (a kind). Connections: part pairs that must touch. Proportions: a part's size relative to a reference (height of the whole object unless 'of' names a part). Layering: back-to-front order hints. Outline: the default outline policy. Build: how to construct one (approach, workflows, operations, organic, shapes, patterns, looks, palette, placements {part, anchor PART.ANCHOR, at?, spread?, side?, mirror?, note?}, guidance, research, checks and a working example batch); its lists merge down the chain with the child's items first, and palette and example are replaced.

approach: Build from soft overlapping masses (ellipse, teardrop, capsule, blob or an organic preset), not boxes; tuck each joint under the part it grows from.
Vary sizes and angles a little (irregular at subtle) so it reads as alive, and keep one light direction across the parts.

constructed.summary: Made things: instruments, vehicles, buildings, furniture, tools, devices and containers.

approach: Build from geometric primitives (rectangle, rounded-rectangle, trapezoid, ellipse) with one corner radius and one stroke weight; unite a silhouette from several shapes with pathfinder.
Keep made things straight and symmetric about their axis; line parts up with align and distribute rather than by eye.

natural.summary: Landscape and weather forms without a fixed anatomy.

approach: Draw one mass with an irregular edge (path, blob or an organic preset), then lighter and darker facets or puffs on top for its form; leave it without an outline.

symbolic.summary: Signs drawn to be read, not depicted: icons, badges, emblems.

approach: Draw one bold silhouette on a square grid, then a few details in one stroke weight; it must still read at 24 px.

texture.summary: Surface patterns (fur, spots, scales, cells). Not objects: apply them to an object's parts.

person.summary: A human figure. A standard character (the character operation) is a person: its character parts read as these parts.

approach: Front view: about 7.5 heads tall, the head about 1/8 of the height, shoulders about 2 heads wide, the crotch at half the height and the hands at mid-thigh.

Draw the 17 standard parts as shapes and bind them with the character operation (its parts map names every part and makes the figure posable), or plan head units with the figure-plan workflow. character without parts draws a cartoon about 3.4 heads tall: declare that object stylized: true.
Limbs overlap at every joint; the torso overlaps the chin and the tops of the arms and legs.

placements.note: the chin overlaps the torso's top
on the eye line, halfway down the head
about a quarter of the head above the chin

research.title: Figure proportions
research.notes: Adult realism: 7 to 8 heads tall; the eyes halfway down the head; shoulders 2 to 2.5 head heights wide; elbows at the waist; wrists and the crotch at half the height; knees a quarter of the height above the soles. Children are 4 to 6 heads tall, mascots 2 to 4.

adult.summary: An adult figure, about 7.5 heads tall.

child.summary: A child figure: a larger head, 4 to 6 heads tall.

mascot-figure.summary: A stylised figure: big head, short limbs, simple features.

animal.summary: An animal: a head and a body, with species-specific limbs.

approach: Block the head and body as overlapping ellipses, then legs as capsules tucked under the body, the tail and the features; draw a side view facing right unless the brief says otherwise.
In a side view the far limbs sit behind the body a shade darker (name them depth far), the near limbs overlap it in front (depth near).
Four legs: the hind and front pairs at about a fifth and four fifths of the body's length.

patterns.note: fur tufts along the body's edge

dog.summary: A dog: snout, floppy or pointed ears, four legs and a tail.

approach: Dog: a long snout ellipse in front of the head, floppy teardrop ears hanging from the top of the head and a tail raised from the rump; the head about half the body's length.

research.title: Dog proportions
research.notes: Shoulder height about 0.8 of the body's length (chest to rump); the head about 0.4 of the body's length and the muzzle about half the head; the legs about half the shoulder height.

cat.summary: A cat: round head, pointed ears, whiskers and a long tail.

approach: Cat: a round head with pointed triangle ears, a short muzzle, whiskers as thin open strokes and a long tail curving up from the rump; a slimmer body than a dog's.

research.title: Cat proportions
research.notes: The head about a third of the body's length; ears about a third of the head's height, set wide; the tail about as long as the body; slim legs about as long as the body is deep.

horse.summary: A horse: long head and neck, mane, four long legs.

rabbit.summary: A rabbit: long ears, round body, short tail.

bear.summary: A bear: heavy body, round ears, short tail.

giraffe.summary: A giraffe: very long neck and legs, patched coat (the giraffe organic preset is its coat texture).

bird.summary: A bird: beak, wings, two legs and tail feathers.

approach: Bird: an egg-shaped body, a round head overlapping its front top, a triangle beak, teardrop wings laid along the body (raised for flight: the far one behind the body) and tail feathers from the rear.

research.title: Bird proportions
research.notes: The head about a third of the body's length; the closed wing covers most of the body's side; the beak names the bird: a short cone for seed eaters, a hook for raptors, a long bill for waders.

fish.summary: A fish: body, fins and a tail fin.

approach: Fish: an ellipse or lens body, the head as its front third, a triangle tail fin at the rear, a dorsal fin on top and a pectoral fin behind the head; one eye near the front.

research.title: Fish anatomy
research.notes: Body depth about a third of its length in most fish; the tail fin about a quarter of the body's length; the eye in the front quarter.

insect.summary: An insect: head, thorax and abdomen, six legs, antennae.

caterpillar.summary: A caterpillar: a head and a chain of round segments.

cephalopod.summary: An octopus or squid: a mantle and arms.

octopus.summary: An octopus: round mantle and eight curling arms.

jellyfish.summary: A jellyfish: a bell and trailing tentacles.

starfish.summary: A starfish: five arms around a centre.

coral.summary: Coral: a branching or folded colony.

brain-coral.summary: Brain coral: a dome with winding grooves.

mollusc.summary: A soft-bodied animal, often with a shell.

snail.summary: A snail: a spiral shell on a soft body with eye stalks.

worm.summary: A worm: a chain of segments.

approach: Grow the plant from its base: the stem or trunk first, then branches and leaves, then flowers or the canopy, each overlapping what it grows from.
An organic preset (flower, tree, leaf, fern …) draws a whole plant in one layer; draw separate shapes when its parts must be named and checked.

tree.summary: A tree: trunk and canopy, optional branches and roots.

approach: Tree: a tapering trunk (trapezoid or path) and a canopy mass (the cloud shape, a blob or overlapping ellipses) whose bottom overlaps the trunk's top; branches tuck under the canopy.

research.title: Tree shapes
research.notes: Broadleaf: a round or oval canopy wider than tall, the trunk a quarter to half of the height; conifer: a cone of tiers with the trunk mostly hidden; palm: a tall curved trunk with a crown of fronds. Trunks taper and flare at the base.

oak.summary: An oak: thick trunk and broad round canopy.

pine.summary: A conifer: a cone-shaped canopy of tiers.

palm.summary: A palm: tall curved trunk and a crown of fronds.

flower.summary: A flower: petals around a centre on a stem.

approach: Flower: petals around a centre disc (ellipses rotated outward, or radial-repeat), a thin stem from the centre down and leaves against the stem.

placements.note: rotated outward at even angles, each overlapping the centre

research.title: Flower structure
research.notes: Petal counts name the flower: 4 or 5 most often, many thin ones for a daisy, spiralled cups for a rose. Petals are alike and evenly spaced; the centre is about a third of the flower head's width.

daisy.summary: A daisy: many thin white petals around a yellow centre.

sunflower.summary: A sunflower: a large seeded centre ringed with yellow petals.

dandelion.summary: A dandelion seed head: a sphere of fine seeds on a stem.

leaf.summary: A single leaf: blade and stalk.

approach: Leaf: a pointed blade (vesica or teardrop), a midrib vein as an open stroke along its axis and a short stalk overlapping the blade's base.

research.title: Leaf anatomy
research.notes: The midrib runs from the stalk to the tip; side veins leave it at 30 to 60 degrees; most blades are 2 to 3 times as long as they are wide.

frond.summary: A frond: a long leaf split into leaflets.

fern.summary: A fern: curling fronds from one base.

grass.summary: Grass blades from a base line.

cactus.summary: A cactus: ribbed body, spines, optional arms, flower and pot.

lily-pad.summary: A floating round leaf with a notch.

mushroom.summary: A mushroom: cap on a stem, optional gills and spots.

approach: Mushroom: a domed cap (semicircle) over a short stem, the gills a darker band under the cap's rim, spots as one group of small ellipses on the cap (mark that group detached_ok).

research.title: Mushroom shapes
research.notes: A fly agaric: a red cap with white spots on a white stem; the cap 1.5 to 2 times as wide as the stem is tall; gills fan out under the rim.

feather.summary: A feather: a shaft with vanes on both sides.

cell.summary: A cell: membrane, nucleus and organelles.

approach: Instrument: a precise silhouette (a pathfinder union of primitives), then the details that name it (strings, keys, a sound hole) in a darker tone; keep it symmetric about its long axis.

guitar.summary: A guitar: body, neck, headstock, strings, sound hole and bridge.

approach: Guitar: the body is two overlapping ellipses (upper and lower bout) united with pathfinder; a sound hole, a bridge on the lower bout, a long neck overlapping the body's top, a headstock overlapping the neck's top and six strings as one open path from the headstock to the bridge, drawn last.

placements.note: on the lower bout, about a fifth of the body's height above its bottom
from the headstock to the bridge

research.title: Guitar anatomy
research.notes: Acoustic: six strings run from the nut at the top of the neck over the sound hole to the bridge; the neck is about 0.5 to 0.7 of the body's height and the headstock about a third of the neck; the lower bout is wider than the upper. An electric guitar has a solid body with pickups instead of a sound hole.

piano.summary: A piano: case, keys and legs.

drum.summary: A drum: shell, head and rims.

vehicle.summary: Something that carries people or goods.

approach: Vehicle: a side view facing right; the body's silhouette first, then the windows, then wheels overlapping the body's bottom edge (depth near; far wheels hidden or darker behind).

car.summary: A car: body, windows and wheels.

approach: Car: a long rounded lower body and a cabin (trapezoid) on top, grouped as the body part; two windows in the cabin, two wheels centred on the body's bottom edge, a headlight at the front.

research.title: Car proportions
research.notes: Wheel diameter about a third of the car's height; the wheelbase about 60% of its length; the cabin starts behind the front wheel and its roof is about half the length.

bicycle.summary: A bicycle: frame, two wheels, handlebar and seat.

boat.summary: A boat: hull, optional mast and sail.

approach: Building: a front view; the walls first, the roof overlapping the walls' top, then doors and windows inside the walls on a grid (distribute).

house.summary: A house: walls, roof, door and windows.

approach: House: a rectangle wall, a triangle roof wider than the wall and overlapping its top, a chimney behind the roof, a door standing on the wall's bottom edge and a window either side.

research.title: House proportions
research.notes: A door is about 2 m tall and half a storey wide; windows sit in a row about a third of the way up the wall; the roof overhangs the walls a little on both sides.

tower.summary: A tall building: shaft and top.

chair.summary: A chair: seat, back and legs.

hammer.summary: A hammer: head on a handle.

approach: Container: the body's silhouette first, the rim or cap at its opening and a handle overlapping the body's side.

cup.summary: A cup: body, rim and handle.

approach: Cup: a body (rounded-rectangle or trapezoid), an ellipse rim across its top, a ring handle overlapping its right side and steam above the rim marked detached_ok (the catalog shapes cup and steam draw a whole mug in one layer each).

placements.note: floats above the rim: mark it layer-intent detached_ok

research.title: Cup proportions
research.notes: A mug is about as wide as it is tall; the handle about half the body's height on its side; steam rises about 0.6 of the cup's height and is narrower than the cup.

bottle.summary: A bottle: body, neck and cap.

pot.summary: A plant pot: body and rim.

rock.summary: A rock: one mass with facets.

approach: Rock: one irregular polygon mass (path or blob) with two or three lighter and darker facets inside it for the lit and shaded planes.

research.title: Rock form
research.notes: A flattish base and an irregular top; with light from one side the top facet is lightest and the side turned away darkest.

cloud.summary: A cloud: overlapping puffs on a flat base.

approach: Cloud: three or four overlapping ellipse puffs over a flat capsule base, all one colour, the largest puff near the middle.

research.title: Cloud shapes
research.notes: Cumulus: a flat base and billowing puffs, the largest near the middle; light tops and slightly darker bases.

water.summary: Water: a surface with waves and highlights.

mountain.summary: A mountain: a peak with an optional snow cap.

sun.summary: A sun: a disc and rays.

icon.summary: An icon: one silhouette on a square grid.

badge.summary: A badge: a shape, a border and a label.

emblem.summary: An emblem: a mark with a frame and a motto.

patches.summary: Irregular patches, like a giraffe's coat.
